title: salvia whitehousei var. parviflora
intro: Salvia whitehousei var. parviflora, commonly known as White House Sage, is a plant species within the Lamiaceae family, characterized by its small, blue-violet flowers and narrow, lance-shaped leaves. The plant has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, offering several health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects, which may help to alleviate symptoms of digestive issues and respiratory problems. The therapeutic actions of Salvia whitehousei var. parviflora include its ability to induce relaxation and reduce anxiety, as well as its potential to improve cognitive function and memory. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, such as rosmarinic acid and salvinic acid, which have been shown to possess antioxidant and neuroprotective properties.
